title: The Spear Hero’s Council of Heroes [Part 2]
text: “I mean, there should only be two people who know how to enhance Ren and Itsuki—doesn’t the fact that you know that prove it?”
“You’re trying to lull me into a false sense of security with that, aren’t you? But it won’t work! You’re the mastermind behind it all!”
For some reason, my Father pointed his finger at me in response to his own question.
“Is that based on your knowledge of the game or something?”
“Ah, that’s right. In *Brave Star Online* quests, there are NPCs with powers as strong as yours. You’ve inherited the power of an NPC designed for story events!”

I was wondering what he was going to say… In MMORPGs, characters with incredibly powerful abilities sometimes appear during events. It’s a setup where, for example, a formidable boss is defeated right in front of the players during an event.

Well, since it’s an event, the boss is often just a stationary NPC, but in terms of appearance, it’s supposed to be one of the strongest bosses in the game. Was there an event where an even stronger enemy—like an event NPC—betrayed the player at the last minute and turned against them after that boss was defeated?

He’s probably just forcing a connection here, claiming that I’ve inherited the power of the event’s mastermind. As for the mastermind hiding inside my weapon… am I overthinking this? Anyway, it seems like that’s the kind of thing he’d be thinking about. There have been similar events, but in my case, it was a character who was actually a good-hearted hero possessed by a boss from the waves.
“That’s impossible. I’ve sworn loyalty to my Father. It’s all for love.”

“Ren, Itsuki, calm down. No matter how strong Motoyasu-kun is, if you think it’s a different weapon spec or that you can’t do it, then you can’t. You can’t pull off this enhancement method unless you believe what the other person is saying.”
“Hmph.”

Ren was trying to check his stats, you know. Itsuki was doing the same. But if you don’t believe in the enhancement method from the bottom of your heart, you won’t be able to pull it off. The problem is that it won’t work if you’re just thinking, “Maybe I can do it.”
“See? You can’t do it after all.”
“You big liar! It seems Motoyasu was the mastermind behind it all! I won’t be manipulated like Naofumi was!”
“You’re making a huge mistake if you think you can control us however you want!”
“It’s not a matter of ‘can’t’ or ‘can.’ I’m saying you can’t do it unless you believe in it. Right now, Ren and Itsuki don’t look like they believe what Motoyasu is saying.”
“Of course not! It’s ridiculous to expect us to trust a lunatic like this!”
“Exactly!”

“Calm down! It doesn’t do you any good to harbor such hostility just because you’ve encountered an opponent who might be stronger than you. Why do you think I, Motoyasu, Ren, and Itsuki were summoned to this world?”

Judging by their expressions, neither Ren nor Itsuki seems the least bit inclined to change their displeased looks at Father’s words. Still, “Why were we summoned?” it is. It’s obvious. It’s to meet Filo-tan. After all, I swore to save the world through my fated encounter with Filo-tan.
“It’s not so you can get stronger and brag about it, is it? We were summoned to save the world. What good does it do to hate and deceive each other in a place like this?”
“I don’t know. But there must be a reason. I’ll be the one to uncover that purpose!”
“Hmph. Don’t get too cocky just because you got a cheat. I’ll definitely prove I’m stronger than you!”

It seems he has no intention of listening to my Father’s words. I could beat him up head-on—just enough to hurt him without killing him—to show off my strength right here, but Father looks like he’s going to stop me.

“Enough is enough. Ren, Itsuki… you two need to really think about why you’re here. Are you here to outsmart someone and prove you’re right? Are you satisfied with making someone the villain and killing someone?”
“You’re trying to elicit sympathy again, aren’t you? We’re not falling for it.”
“That’s right. You’re trying to lure us in by playing on our sympathy so you can take over this world, aren’t you?”

My Father let out a sigh that sounded like he was thoroughly fed up with Ren and Itsuki’s responses. I agree with him. What’s the point of conquering a world like this, anyway? In fact, the very fact that they’re saying things like that suggests that’s exactly what Ren and Itsuki want to do, doesn’t it?
“You can only get cocky for so long. I’ll catch up to you guys in no time.”
“That’s right. Just because you’ve gotten a little stronger doesn’t mean you can stay cocky forever. Eventually, we’ll see who’s right.”

“Are you trying to say you’re the one who’s right? This isn’t the time to be arguing over trivialities like who’s right or wrong. Motoyasu-kun is losing in the future, isn’t he? A threat powerful enough to defeat Motoyasu-kun is closing in. We don’t have the luxury of time to be fighting amongst ourselves in this world.”
Father pleaded desperately, but Ren and Itsuki wouldn’t listen, replying:
“Looks like there’s nothing to be gained from this conversation.”
“That’s right. Excuse us. Listening to the cheat methods of people who rely on unfair power would just rot our ears.”
This is getting tiresome. Neither Ren nor Itsuki are the type who can be swayed by persuasion.
“Do you really think that weapon—the one we’ll face after we’re done leveling up on this island—will give us a visible boost in strength?”
Maybe I should make my move first here? Ren and Itsuki turned around, looking annoyed. I hit the nail on the head.

Back in the first world, after I left Cal Mira Island, I was so full of myself that I thought I’d gain even more incredible power. I struggled against the Pope, but I thought that with that weapon, I’d be more than twice as strong as I am now… That’s what I believed back then. I really did think that even though the boss was weak, it dropped something exceptional.

The Spirit Tortoise’s rare weapon is superior to any weapon I’d gotten from shops or monster materials up to that point. Back in the MMO days, Spirit Tortoise rare weapons were famous for fetching high prices on the market. Of course, they’re inferior compared to the other Four Spirits, but they’re the bare minimum you need to hunt the next Four Spirits. Well, if you try hard enough, you might be able to win without one, but it’d be tough unless you level up quite a bit.

“You’re probably thinking the Spirit Tortoise is weak and would make a good starting point, so let me stop you right there. That thing is a monster that Ren and Itsuki can’t even begin to handle at their current levels.”
In the game, it was an easy opponent to take on. I thought we’d have plenty of leeway in terms of level… That’s why I was convinced when I heard that Ren and Itsuki had broken the seal.

Of course… it’s also true that I was completely wrong. In reality, the weapons crafted from the Spirit Tortoise’s materials had lower stats than the ones in the MMO. Though, apparently, Father’s shield and Ren’s sword were excellent. Ren told me those were actually new weapons he’d forged from scratch using those materials.
“I’ll say it as many times as it takes. You’d better not challenge the Spirit Tortoise. As long as I’m still alive, I’ll stop you no matter what.”
“Motoyasu…”
This is my resolve. And it is also my regret.

There have been days when I’ve regretted over and over again that, back then, I foolishly broke the Spirit Tortoise’s seal. Of course, one could say that it was precisely because I was defeated by the Spirit Tortoise that I awakened to true love—but that doesn’t give me a reason not to stop it if I have a chance to do it over.
“Hmph. So you’re trying to stop us from getting stronger, are you?”
“You’re trying to monopolize our strength. How despicable!”
“The secret to our strength is the training method Father taught me. There’s not a word of lies in what I’m saying.”
“How much longer do you plan to interfere before you’re satisfied?! Seriously, this meeting was a complete waste of time!”
“Exactly! I don’t have time to put up with your selfishness!”
The two of them stand up and are about to leave the room.
“Ren, Itsuki, right now we’re both so worked up that we might not be able to listen to each other. But I want you to hear just this one thing.”
“Is there still something else?”
“Hmph.”

“This world certainly has levels, stats, and enhancement methods. We’re under the illusion that it’s like a game, but for the people living in this world, this is reality. That doesn’t change even for monsters. Everyone has only one life.”

My Father was stating the obvious. Well, back then, I used to think it was okay if I got killed. I had this mysterious confidence that even if I died, I’d just be revived at the healing clinic. Logically speaking, since this isn’t inside a game, if you die, that’s the end of it. The fact that we’re stuck in this loop is a miracle, after all.
“Another lecture? Give it a rest already.”
“Why do I have to be scolded for defeating a vicious dragon?”
“No, that’s not it. I’m not objecting to you defeating monsters. I’m saying this because if you treat life and death like a game, it could lead to something irreversible.”

Something irreversible… like the victims of the Spirit Tortoise! And then there’s the plague from the dragon’s carcass, right? If things keep going this way, Ren and Itsuki are bound to revive the Spirit Tortoise and do something irreversible. Of course, I’ll stop them, and even if it is revived, I’ll defeat it before any damage is done.

Still, Father’s words—I feel like I’ve heard them somewhere before. Ah… I think my Rival said something like that in the first world, or maybe Father was warning Ren about it. I was there, so I remember it well.

Apparently, the Rival was furious that Ren had killed him just for fun—something along those lines. Since that dragon was wild, it wasn’t actually angry about being killed itself. In that sense, the Rival had seen right through the fact that we were treating it like a game.

Also, my Father mentioned something about “the survival of the fittest,” didn’t he? Something about how treating it like a game is wrong. In other words, if you’re going to kill, you have to be prepared to take a life.

Come to think of it, Ren was much calmer back then than he is now. When fighting monsters, he’d say things like, “Is this also an exchange of lives…?”—sounds like typical middle-schooler nonsense. I suppose he resonated with what Father and the Assistant said. But it seems those words don’t reach the Ren of today at all.
“Hmph, what’s wrong with defeating enemies? How I fight is my business.”
“You’re just spouting vague nonsense—I don’t understand a word of it.”
Ren stormed out of the room looking annoyed, and Itsuki followed right behind him. And so, the meeting between the heroes ended with results that seemed even worse than those in the first world.
“Sigh…”
My father lets out a deep sigh.

“I never imagined he’d be that stubborn… It would be a little better if he at least believed in the enhancement method, but he won’t listen at all—and on top of that, he’s going around saying Motoyasu-kun is the mastermind behind it all…”
“There’s nothing we can do about it.”

“Well, when you’re summoned to another world and called a hero, it’s natural to think you’re the protagonist. I have that tendency to some extent myself, so maybe he’s panicking because Motoyasu’s overwhelming strength makes him realize he might not be the protagonist after all.”
“That’s right. Ren and Itsuki are mistaken. You’re the protagonist, Father!”
“Hmph…”
At my words, my father’s face twitched as if he were exasperated. Did I say something strange?
“It’s not that… It’s just, when you see yourself as the protagonist, if someone overwhelmingly stronger than you shows up, thinking of them as nothing but an enemy is a bit…”
“Ah, I see. It’s the classic trope: if an opponent is higher level than you, they either die or betray you! Hahaha!”
“That’s not funny!?”
Hahaha, so basically, my Father and I will either die as sacrifices for Ren and Itsuki, Or we’ll betray them and turn against them. I’m sure that’s how he’s thinking.
“Um… Naofumi-sama. How should I go about delivering this message?”
My fiancée asks, placing a hand on my Father’s shoulder as he looks dejected.
“For now, as I’m sure Melty-chan heard, just make sure Ren and Itsuki don’t go to the place where the Spirit Tortoise is sealed.”
“Yes, I understand.”
“I hope it goes well.”

“Yeah. Well, the meeting was a failure for now, but later on, we’ll work on something… an event to persuade Ren and Itsuki… and address the issues on Faubrey. Of course, after we’ve made sure to keep a tight rein on Ren and Itsuki, that is.”
Father stands up with an exhausted expression and leaves the room. I follow him.
“Since we can’t use portals on Cal Mira Island while it’s being revitalized, Ren and the others won’t just suddenly disappear.”
“Hearing that puts my mind at ease… I guess. For now, I’ll have to do my best to make peace with Ren and Itsuki.”

Saying this, my Father, with a slightly weary smile, continued speaking. I think it’ll be difficult at that rate. Still, if I give up like that, everything will become meaningless. For the sake of the peaceful world I promised to Filo-tan, I’ll overcome any hardship.
“For now, let’s relax on the island and unwind to recover from our fatigue. We’ve got a long road ahead of us, after all.”
“That’s right! Finally, we can start looking for the Filolial-sama’s eggs… I mean, Filo-tan’s egg.”
When I said this cheerfully, my Father gave a wry smile.
“Motoyasu-kun, you’re full of energy, aren’t you? You’ve got such strong mental fortitude—it’s hard to believe you’ve been through so many loops.”
“What are you talking about? If the number of Filolial-sama and the others increases, I believe we’ll be able to handle even the worst-case scenario.”
“Well… if the worst does happen, having more people on hand might help minimize the damage.”
“Exactly.”

Even if Ren and Itsuki were to break the Spirit Tortoise’s seal, I’m sure my Father and I could quickly handle the situation and limit the damage to a minimum. Even Ren and Itsuki would surely realize their own foolishness if they were defeated by the Spirit Tortoise. Of course, I’ll do my utmost to prevent that from happening.
“So, Father, you should try to relax a little.”
“…You’re right. Even if Ren and Itsuki go out of control, we’ll just have to figure it out somehow. Afterward, we can persuade them just like my future self did, right?”
My Father’s expression brightened slightly.
“Melty-chan, please be prepared for the worst-case scenario.”
“Yes. I’ll let Mother know.”
“Please do.”
And so, the meeting between the heroes for this loop came to an end. Starting tomorrow, we’ll begin training Filolial-sama. I’m so excited I might not even be able to sleep tonight! Filo~ta~n!
